The planner first maximizes the total length of placed parts, then the number of parts, then reduces used raw-stock length and stock count. Larger tasks use a bounded search and are not guaranteed optimal.
%1$d parts • saw loss %2$s mm • remainder %3$s mm
These parts are too long or the available stock is insufficient for the found plan. They are not included in the diagrams or totals.
Blue: parts • amber: saw loss • grey: end trim and remainder

Plan straight cuts from lengths of the same material and cross section, using finite stock quantities. All dimensions are in millimetres.

Trim is deducted at both ends, and includes any loss from making those end cuts. The saw kerf is reserved between parts and before a remaining offcut. When the last part ends exactly at the usable stock end, no extra final kerf is reserved.

Diagrams are scaled; the written lengths and start/end positions are the measurements. Unplaced parts remain listed. Plans do not mix materials, model angled cuts, or nest sheet panels.

Small tasks receive complete search when it finishes within the limit. Larger tasks show the best found plan. The objective is total placed length, then placed count, then less raw stock and fewer stock pieces.

Drafts and saved projects stay on this device. Sharing sends a CSV only to the app you choose. Editing inputs invalidates the old result.
